designRationale.howTheSplitOfCHFWasDrawn: NOT by re-quoting the frozen section 12 stage table - Agent E proved that reproducing the contract's own decomposition carries no independent evidential weight (E-SC-1), and this design withdraws that convergence claim. The split is drawn on three independent axes that the contract does not supply: (1) REVERSIBILITY - ingestion decisions are cheap to correct, custody decisions are irreversible and founder-gated, presentation decisions are client-side and reversible; (2) REPOSITORY AND WORK KIND - CH-11 and CH-12 are backend/infrastructure with EXTERNAL_INFRASTRUCTURE and PB-11 dependencies, CH-13 is client work under a founder-frozen hard gate; (3) GATE VISIBILITY - placing F016 in CH-11 while the findings it gates (F011/F014/F015) sit in CH-13 makes the gate cross a chapter boundary, so it can no longer be silently absorbed by the chapter it gates. The resulting boundaries happen to be compatible with the frozen chain, which is a constraint they must satisfy, not evidence that they are right.
unitAssignmentRules: RULE 1 - A finding is owned by the chapter that owns the system which must become correct for it to stop recurring. Exactly one owner. Cross-references are recorded and never counted as ownership.
RULE 2 - A chartered obligation is owned by the chapter that must DO it or PROVE it.

RULE 3 - A FROZEN_OUTCOME obligation whose content is a constraint on future work is owned by the chapter that owns the authority it froze; it appears as a protectedBoundary or nonGoal in every other chapter it constrains.
RULE 4 - A CHARTERED_SCOPE:preserve obligation is owned by the chapter that would otherwise break it.
RULE 5 - A historicalItems obligation (roadmap Items 1-17) is owned by the chapter that continues that item's work.

RULE 8 - Where charter ownership and implementation ownership legitimately differ, the obligation is owned by the IMPLEMENTING chapter and the charter relationship is stated explicitly. This is the founder's ruling, not an invention, and it never creates a duplicate programme.

RULE 9 - No obligation and no finding may be assigned to more than one chapter. continuityResolution.verdict: DEDICATED CHAPTER - CH-02 Continuity & Destination Authority. It is neither distributed across existing chapters nor force-fitted into an RC chapter to remove an orphan.
evidenceForADedicatedChapter: Sixteen findings spanning six unrelated product surfaces resolve to TWO shared causes (F065 session-state establishment fragmented across call sites; F069 route classification maintained as a hand-kept fail-OPEN allowlist). A cause set that produces defects on six surfaces is a system, not a per-surface bug class.
REFRESH IS NOT NAVIGATION is a founder-frozen PLATFORM CONTRACT with no implementing authority. Contracts without authorities are the failure shape this programme exists to end.

No RC chapter charters it, and the reason is structural rather than accidental: four chapters touch continuity and three of them touch it as PRESERVATION (RC-C1 preserve session handling, RC-C3 preserve session continuity, RC-C5 preserve drafts) while RC-C9 touches it as a platform build item. Preserving a thing is an instruction NOT to reconstruct it.

Chronology confirms it: the roadmap froze 2026-08-15; the continuity contract froze 2026-08-17. The reconstruction axis could not have chartered an authority whose governing contract did not yet exist.

Distribution was tested and rejected: if each surface chapter owned its own continuity findings, each would build its own destination reconstruction and its own session-state reading. That is the temporary architecture the chapter test forbids, and it is the observed cause of the sixteen findings.

The chapter therefore does not claim that no finding in the cluster has any recorded RC relationship; it claims that no chapter charters the AUTHORITY, which remains true.

f137OwnerAndProof.finding: F137 - the moderation service is text-only; NO uploaded media of any kind is scanned. Founder classification: ZERO_COVERAGE_SECURITY_GAP.
f137OwnerAndProof.ownershipTestUsed: Which system's responsibility boundary must change for an uploaded object to be examined at all, and for that examination to have a consequence? Not: which chapter's name contains a matching word.
proof: AN EXAMINATION IS AN OPERATION OVER A STORED OBJECT. It is asynchronous, it runs after the bytes exist, and it must also cover objects uploaded BEFORE it existed. The only chapter that owns an asynchronous pipeline over stored originals, plus the backfill posture for the existing population, is the custody and processing chapter - it already owns derivative generation, EXIF stripping and the reconciliation cohorts.

A VERDICT IS ONLY REAL IF IT GATES DELIVERY. F138 establishes that the delivery boundary today performs no authorization of any kind and that possession of a key or a historical URL IS access. A scanner whose verdict cannot stop bytes reaching a viewer is theatre. The delivery decision is owned by CH-12 and by nothing else.

A VERDICT ALSO GATES RETENTION. Quarantine, hold and removal are retention states over the same object, and the retention authority - with its isRetentionEligible() asymmetry and its D-6 seven-step order - lives in CH-12. Splitting verdicts from retention would create a second actor able to influence deletion, which is precisely the F143 hazard (logical decision authorising physical consequence) in a new place.

INGESTION SUPPLIES AN INPUT, NOT THE HOME. CH-11 establishes the resolved type class the scanner needs, and rejects at the door - but presign-time rejection is synchronous and per-door, and F129 proves the doors are still plural. A scan bound to one ingestion door would miss objects by construction.
PRESENTATION CONSUMES ACCESS STATE AND NEVER DECIDES IT (the frozen client-primitive rule), so CH-13 cannot own it.

A DEDICATED SAFETY CHAPTER WOULD MANUFACTURE TEMPORARY ARCHITECTURE. To act, it would need its own storage lifecycle, ingestion choke point, derivative worker and delivery gate - four systems CH-12 already owns. The chapter test forbids exactly this.

THE MODERATION CHAPTER IS THE WORD-SIMILARITY TRAP AND IS REFUSED. CH-15 owns no storage lifecycle, no delivery boundary, no worker and no ingestion door. Assigning F137 there would satisfy the vocabulary and defer the capability.
f137OwnerAndProof.whatCH15OwnsInstead: The POLICY and the CONSEQUENCE: what a positive verdict means, whether the object is quarantined or removed, what the uploader and the viewer are told, how a false positive is appealed, and how an automated verdict relates to a human report. CH-12 cannot build the mechanism against an undefined policy, so CH-15's policy freeze precedes CH-12's implementation. This is a named dependency, not shared ownership.

scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.maliciousFileAndContentScanning: Owned by CH-12 as an asynchronous verdict pipeline covering every stored object, including a backfill over the existing population.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.mediaSafetyAndModeration: Mechanism CH-12; policy, adjudication and appeal CH-15; in-Live surface CH-09 consuming CH-15.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.imageVideoAudioDocumentImplications: Each kind needs a different examination and a different failure mode; the per-kind capability registry is CH-11's resolved type class, consumed by CH-12. Documents (PDF/DOCX/PPTX) are the highest-risk and least-covered kind and are also the kind F016 shows the product does not yet honestly understand.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.storageLifecycle: CH-12. Quarantine is a retention state, and the isRetentionEligible() asymmetry must hold for it: uncertain may KEEP, never DELETE.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.privacy: CH-12 - the same pipeline that strips EXIF (F132) and mirrors preview imagery into custody (F135). Scanning must not itself become a disclosure: third-party providers would receive private user content, which is why provider selection is a founder act.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.providerVersusSelfHosting: The provider-independence doctrine applies: a self-hosted tier-0 default is required and external providers are optional tier-1 enrichment, never load-bearing. Recorded as a constraint on CH-12, not as a selection.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.falsePositivesAndAppeals: CH-15 owns the appeal route and the consequence ladder; CH-12 must make a verdict reversible in effect, which means quarantine must be a reversible state and never a deletion.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.existingMimeAndContentTruthBoundaries: The 28-type MIME policy remains the single source of PERMISSION (CH-11). A scan verdict is a separate axis from permission: a permitted type may still be refused delivery. Collapsing the two would let a scanner silently redefine the accepted-format policy.
scopeConfrontedAsTheFounderRequired.asynchronousProcessing: CH-12. An upload must not block on examination, and an unexamined object must not be deliverable - which makes the interim state an explicit, product-visible one rather than an implicit gap.

f137OwnerAndProof.authorizes: NOTHING. No implementation, no architecture selection, no provider choice. This records an owner and the boundary that justifies it.
